headline: Data Centers Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, primarily data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and transmission infrastructure, reducing the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Spanberger's administration, consumer advocacy groups, residential ratepayers, environmental advocates.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: SCC Orders Data Centers Pay Grid Costs
news_summary: After Governor Spanberger's push, the State Corporation Commission ordered data centers to cover the full cost of transmission infrastructure built exclusively for their facilities. This decision is projected to save Virginia families hundreds of millions of dollars on their electric bills.

headline: Mandates Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, increasing transparency on their water usage and environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, including SB 553, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency regarding the significant water consumption by data centers, especially as groundwater supplies dwindle.

headline: Local Control Data Center Siting
short_summary: This bill empowers local governments to require site assessments for large data centers, including studies on noise impacts and other environmental effects, before approving new facilities.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data centers, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Virginia Law Requires Data Center Site Assessments
news_summary: HB 153, now law, requires local governments to mandate site assessments for new high energy use facilities (HEUF) like data centers, focusing on noise profiles for nearby homes and schools. Localities can also require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources, giving them more control over data center siting.
